description:
What Would You Send to Aliens?

Episode 85 of a daily journey through the universe. 📀
The Voyager Golden Records, launched in 1977 on Voyager 1 and 2: greetings in 55 languages, 115 images, sounds of Earth and 90 minutes of music, with instructions for playing them, now drifting between the stars.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 86: Next stop, dark matter. The invisible stuff holding galaxies together.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

Images: NASA (public domain)
Narration: AI voice

#space #goldenrecord #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: If you could send one message to aliens, what would it be? NASA already sent one.
In nineteen seventy-seven, two Voyager spacecraft launched to explore the giant planets, and then leave the solar system forever.
segments.headline: Voyager, 1977

segments.text: Each one carries a gold-plated copper record. A message, in case anyone ever finds it.
segments.headline: A golden record

segments.text: A team led by astronomer Carl Sagan chose what to put on it: a portrait of life on Earth.
segments.headline: Chosen by Carl Sagan's team

segments.text: One hundred fifteen images, and about ninety minutes of music from around the world.
Sounds of Earth too: wind, thunder, birds, whales, laughter, a kiss, and a mother with her baby.
segments.headline: Sounds of Earth

segments.text: The cover shows, in symbols, how to play the record and where Earth is, using pulsars as a map.
segments.headline: Instructions included

segments.text: Both Voyagers are now in interstellar space. In about forty thousand years, Voyager one will pass near another star. It's still far, far away from it.
segments.headline: Forever drifting

segments.text: Tomorrow, the invisible matter that outweighs everything we can see. Next stop: dark matter. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for tomorrow's stop.
